# C011 fleet run diagnostic — what the harness did, and what the model did (2026-08-25/26)

**Kind:** measurement artifact — **no runtime code.** Not read at skill runtime.
**Generated by:** claude-opus-5
**Subject run:** one `/wf:fleet NEU-893` invocation over a 16-child tracker umbrella
(C011 research package), shipped end-to-end to 16 merged pull requests.
**Companions:** [fleet-run-token-accounting.md](./fleet-run-token-accounting.md) — the cost
baseline method · [wf-token-leak-inventory.md](./wf-token-leak-inventory.md) — the defect
inventory that baseline exposed.

The run reports **16/16 merged, zero retries, 100% ceremony compliance**. The deliverable is
real and independently verified. The compliance figure is not: `/wf:ship` ran zero times to
completion, and the delivery tail of every item was executed by hand outside the harness.

**The headline finding is neither.** The run executed **wf 0.116.0 from the plugin cache
while `main` was already at 0.117.0** — a version whose sole content is the fix for the exact
branch-gate bug all 16 shippers worked around. The fix merged **33 minutes before the run
started** and was never installed. Nothing in the run reads or reports the resolved plugin
version, so an 11-hour run hard-coded already-fixed defects into all 16 dispatch briefs.

## 2. Method — and what was verified independently

The orchestrator's own narration is unusually candid, which makes it tempting to summarize.
This diagnostic deliberately separates three tiers:

| Tier | How it was obtained | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| **Mechanical** | Counted from transcript JSON — tool-use blocks, agent metadata, timestamps | Every count in §3–§4 |
| **Independently verified** | Re-checked against `git`, `gh`, and the Linear MCP outside the run's reporting | Delivery outcome, merge shapes, breadcrumb, package size |
| **Run-reported** | Taken from the orchestrator's or a shipper's own claim | Defect counts, verify verdicts, brief-error count — **labelled as such throughout** |

Extraction was scripted rather than read: the session JSONL was flattened to a skeleton
(assistant text, tool name + truncated input, truncated tool result, timestamp), each of the
16 shipper transcripts flattened the same way, and agent metadata joined into a spawn tree.
Full transcripts were never read end-to-end — 110 MB of subagent transcript will not fit a
context window, and reading a sample and generalizing is how a diagnostic invents its own
findings.

**Independently verified facts:**

- 16/16 children `Done` in Linear (`list_issues parentId=NEU-893`).
- Package on trunk: 78 files under `docs/research/C011-safe-production-integration-and-learner-isolation/`.
- Merge shapes: 14 squash, **2 merge commits** (#796 `56bd7b6`, #797 `eb099ec`), whose
  intermediate WIP and sync commits are visible on `develop`.
- `origin/develop:.current-task` reads **`NEU-1004`** — one PR leaked a breadcrumb onto trunk.
- 18 registered worktrees still live in the subject repo.
- The `db:studio:prod` finding: `package.json:48` does ship
  `"dotenv -e .env.prod -- drizzle-kit studio"`.

## 4. Which wf surfaces actually executed

Counted from `Skill` tool-use blocks across all 99 transcripts:

| Skill | Invocations | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `wf:run` | 15 | always `--step`, always once; the hands-off walk was never used |
| `wf:triage` | 14 | completed normally |
| `wf:spec` | 13 | completed normally |
| `wf:plan` | 10 | completed normally |
| `wf:verify-spec` | 10 | completed normally |
| `wf:qa-gen` | 10 | completed normally, engine unconfigured |
| `wf:tf` | 4 | read, then performed by hand |
| `wf:implement` | 2 | authoring happened in-context in the other 14 |
| `wf:ship` | **1** | abandoned after Phase 1 |
| `wf:pr` | **1** | abandoned at Phase 3 |
| `wf:index` | 1 | |
| `wf:commit` | **0** | |
| `wf:branch` | **0** | forbidden by the dispatch brief |
| `wf:tasks` / `wf:tt` / `wf:qa-auto` / `wf:verify-fix` | **0** | |

**The delivery tail of all 16 items ran outside the harness.** Every commit, push, PR creation,
check poll, merge, and finalize was a raw `git`/`gh` invocation composed by the shipper.

Artifacts produced (per-worktree `_local/{ID}/`, plus 4 archived by `wf:tf`):

- **16/16** complete sets of `00_reqs` · `01_spec` · `02_plan` · `04_verify` · `06_qa`.
- `03_tasks.md`: **0** — `wf:phase-runner` supports only triage/spec/plan/verify-spec/qa-gen,
  so `wf:tasks` is orphaned from every automated path.
- `index.md`: **8/16** — the per-task index convention lapsed in half the items.
- `05_verify-fix` / `07_qa-report`: 1 each (NEU-1007).

Artifact **quality** is high and the wf templates are visibly the reason: `NEU-1003/04_verify.md`
is a 12-criterion conformance table with file-and-line evidence per row — and it was
**hand-authored**, since that shipper never invoked `wf:verify-spec`. The format discipline
propagated where the executor did not.

## 5. Failures

**F1 — The branch gate blocks the entire delivery tail (16/16).** `wf:commit`, `wf:tf` and
`wf:branch` in 0.116.0 test for a literal `/{numeric-id}-` substring, which cannot match
`feat/NEU-993-…`. Every shipper detected this and routed around it. Fixed on `main` in 0.117.0
— see §8.

**F2 — `/wf:ship` cannot drive its own chain under fleet dispatch.** Invoked once (NEU-993),
abandoned immediately: its build chain dispatches `wf:phase-runner` as a subagent whose cwd
resolves to the shared checkout, where the task folder does not exist. Triage then returns
blocked and the chain **can fall through to `/wf:pr` → `/wf:tf`, skipping every gate**. A
gate-skipping fallback is the most damaging possible failure mode for a gate-centric harness.

**F3 — `/wf:pr` abandoned at Phase 3** (NEU-996) for the same subagent-cwd reason. PR creation
and tracker linking were completed natively.

**F4 — The resolver defeats worktree isolation.** `resolve_config({workspaceRoot:
".../.claude/worktrees/neu-1003"})` returns `"workspaceRoot":"/workspace/second-memory-mcp"` —
the shared checkout. Reproduced in every shipper. `skills/fleet/SKILL.md:21` instructs agents
to use their own worktree root and never inherit a parent's; the resolver overrides exactly
that. Had any skill trusted the returned root for a write, 16 concurrent shippers would have
written into one tree.

**F5 — Runtime worktree isolation unavailable; the skill's own dispatch shape was not used.**
`skills/fleet/SKILL.md:158` mandates `subagent_type: general-purpose`, `isolation: "worktree"`,
`run_in_background: true`. All 16 dispatches used `subagent_type: "claude"` with **no**
`isolation` and no `run_in_background`. Recorded rationale (scoreboard §"ENVIRONMENT — worktree
isolation"): the runtime evaluates the *container* directory as the worktree root and git
discovers the parent checkout above it; `EnterWorktree` was denied in two shapes. Isolation
ended up **shipper-enforced by hand-written `git worktree add`**, not runtime-enforced.

**F6 — `resolve_routing` produced 20 calls and zero decisions.** Breakdown: 16 accepted
singleton `dispatch` decisions, 2 `invalid-stop` shape rejections (singleton normalization —
`composite` with `unitCount: 1`, then `unitsIndependent: true` with `unitCount: 1`), 1 hard
schema error (`basis` exceeded 256 characters), and 1 three-item composite that returned
`status: "dispatch"` **with `effectiveParallelism: 1`** — a self-contradictory response the
skill's own rule reads as "dispatch nothing under that decision". Every accepted decision
returned what the orchestrator already intended (opus / isolated). No `postAttempt` gate ever
opened. Cost: 20 MCP round-trips and ~600 lines of scoreboard ledger for zero influence on the
run.

**F7 — Orchestrator context exhausted before the first dispatch.** One compaction at
18:00:39, **7 m 18 s into the run**, after reading the fleet body, 16 tracker issues and the
charter. `/context` immediately after showed **73.7 k tokens (27% of a 272 k window) consumed
by deferred MCP tool schemas alone**. The remaining 11 hours ran from a compaction summary plus
the scoreboard, and produced (run-reported) **25 factually wrong claims across 16 dispatch
briefs** — stale spike totals, a phantom `CAP-S1-3`, a wrong escapee list carried into three
briefs. All were caught by shippers reading source, none by the harness.

**F8 — Process artifacts are stranded.** `_local/` was mirrored into each worktree by `cp -r`,
so 15 of 16 task artifact sets exist only inside disposable worktrees. Exactly one shipper
(NEU-1000, 00:04) copied its folder back to the shared `_local/_archive/` — violating its own
"never touch the shared checkout" instruction to do so. `_local/INDEX.md` carries no row for
any of the 16.

## 6. Successes

**S1 — The fan-out loop itself worked.** 10 waves, 16 items, dependency order respected, zero
merge collisions across a shared 8-register band written by 14 concurrent authors, zero stalls,
zero retries, zero replacement spawns.

**S2 — Merge verification was not taken on trust.** The orchestrator re-verified every merge
commit on `origin/develop` itself rather than accepting a shipper's report — and in one case
(NEU-1007) initially contradicted a true shipper claim, then found its own check wrong (it had
grepped the shared checkout's working tree, which was behind trunk) and withdrew the accusation.

**S3 — Inert degradation is real.** `qa-execution:engine` unconfigured → every `06_qa.md`
states it and claims no pass. `wf-audit` unregistered → verify reported "capability findings:
none (no-op path confirmed)". No capability term surfaced anywhere and nothing was fabricated.
This is Core Article 8 behaving exactly as specified.

**S4 — PARTIAL was allowed to mean something.** Run-reported 6 of 16 shipped at
`VERIFY — PARTIAL`, in every case because the unmet criterion required asserting a production
observation that does not exist (no `DATABASE_URL`, no `SMOKE_PROD_*`, no token ever observed).
Shippers registered findings plus unmet gates and shipped visibly rather than certifying green.
A 16/16 PASS would have been the suspicious result.

**S5 — Constitution carriage works.** The SessionStart hook does not fire in a dispatched
worktree shipper (WF-335); the skill's workaround — read `_local/constitution.md` once, carry it
verbatim in every prompt — landed in all 16 and was observably honoured. No AI attribution in
any commit or PR body; no `main` commits.

**S6 — Closeout led with the failure.** The audit declared the package's completeness gate
**not met** (15 met / 2 met-with-cap / 2 n/a / **2 not met**) and that verdict opens the
umbrella's resolution comment rather than being buried under the 16/16 line.

## 7. Gaps — expected but structurally unavailable

**G1 — The gate model does not survive unattended mode.** Core Article 2 (*"every phase is a
human-approved artifact; nothing advances past an unapproved gate"*) was carried verbatim into
all 16 shipper prompts, while `/wf:ship`'s own description says it *"drives the `wf:*` build
chain **past the gates** where `/wf:run` halts."* Zero approvals occurred in 11 hours. No agent
flagged the contradiction. Either fleet mode needs explicit self-approval semantics, or Article
2 needs a stated exception.

**G2 — `SHIP —` is unfalsifiable proof.** `/wf:fleet` treats a pasted `SHIP —`/`TF —` block as
ceremony evidence. `/wf:ship` completed zero times, so all 16 blocks were composed by the agent
whose compliance they attest to. NEU-1007's block says so in its own text: *"phases run
natively; `/wf:ship`'s chain not used."* The run's "ceremony compliance 100%" measures string
presence.

**G3 — The review layer that caught everything is not wf's.** 13 hand-rolled adversarial
subagents found a run-reported **353 defects** before merge, including a pre-flight predicate
bounding chunk difficulty at `1–5` where the codebase defines `1–10` — forwarded as a
**migration abort condition**, i.e. it would have aborted a live migration on healthy data —
and an unlisted assumption that would have voided a chapter's central derivation. External
review (Copilot) approved the same PRs with 0 comments. wf's own `verify` phase caught none of
them. This practice was invented ad hoc by the orchestrator, mandated in prompts, and leaves no
trace in the harness.

**G4 — Tracker dependency edges do not exist.** All 16 children returned empty
`blockedBy`/`blocks`; `/wf:charter`'s child creation writes title, team, parent and description
but no relation records. The entire 16-edge graph was orchestrator-derived from
`02_subtasks.md`. Read literally, all 16 would have been ready at once — and positions 15–16
consume every prior chapter.

**G5 — The delivery contract has no worktree vocabulary.** `capabilities/git/fragments/delivery.ops.md`
(0.7.1) ships branch/commit/push/pr/merge plus reads — and no `worktree-create`. The fleet
architecture is worktree-based, so raw `git worktree add` is necessarily baked into every
dispatch prompt, outside the provider abstraction the skill claims to run through.

## 8. The version-staleness finding

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Harness executed | wf **0.116.0** (plugin cache; highest cached version) |
| `main` at run time | wf **0.117.0** |
| 0.117.0's content | PR **#276** — *"479: Branch gate matches only the numeric id, so tracker-prefixed branches fail it"*, squash-merged `69cf868` |
| Merged at | 2026-08-25 **17:20:04Z** |
| Fleet run started | 2026-08-25 **17:53:21** — 33 minutes later |
| Result | 16/16 shippers worked around a defect already fixed on `main` |

The fix touches `agents/branch.md`, `agents/commit.md`, `agents/pr.md`, `skills/branch`,
`skills/commit`, `skills/tf`, and `skills/_shared/pipeline-conventions.md`; the gate now accepts
`/{task-id}-` **or** `/{numeric-id}-`, compared case-insensitively (`agents/commit.md:42`) —
precisely the `feat/NEU-993-…` shape that failed 16 times.

**The transferable defect is not the branch gate.** It is that `/wf:fleet` never resolves or
reports the plugin version it is running, so a superseded harness executes silently and its
known-bug workarounds propagate into every dispatch brief as if they were current truth. A
single Prerequisites step — resolve the installed wf version, stamp it in the scoreboard
header, warn when it trails the marketplace — would have caught this within 30 seconds of a
run that then went on for 11 hours.

## 9. Corrections made during this diagnostic

Recorded because the same claims appear in the run's own narration and in the first pass of
this analysis:

1. **"Fix #479 is the top-leverage item."** Stale — it was merged before the run started. The
   top-leverage item is version reporting (§8).
2. **"The run is an open reproduction of #479."** It is a reproduction of a **0.116.0** bug, not
   of an open defect.
3. **"The run masks failure as success."** Half true and worth stating precisely: the *prose*
   disclosed the failures prominently (not-met gate first, 25 orchestrator errors counted in
   public, every PARTIAL named). The *summary metrics* did not — "ceremony compliance 100%" and
   "execution efficiency 100%" measure whether the agent typed the right string and whether
   anything independent could have failed it. Nothing could.
4. **The deliverable is not fabricated.** Verified outside the run's reporting: 78 files on
   trunk, 16 PRs merged, 16 issues `Done`, sampled artifacts substantive.

## 10. Not re-tested this run

Every item here was inherited as lore from the prior C010 fleet run, written into the dispatch
briefs as a prohibition, and therefore **never exercised** — its current status is unknown:

- The `wf:phase-runner` cwd fallback (F2) — forbidden by brief, never triggered.
- `Agent(isolation: "worktree")` (F5) — explicitly recorded as "has not been re-tested".
- `EnterWorktree` — not attempted.
- `/wf:branch`'s base switch checking out trunk — never invoked.

Any of these may already be fixed on `main`, exactly as F1 was. A diff of `main` against the
cached 0.116.0 for these specific behaviours is the cheapest next step.

## 11. Recommendations, ranked by leverage

1. **Report the resolved plugin version at fleet/ship Prerequisites** and warn when it trails
   the marketplace. Prevents the whole class in §8. *(core, cheap)*
2. **Make the ceremony block machine-emitted rather than agent-typed**, or `/wf:fleet` can never
   distinguish a run from a claim (G2).
3. **Resolver: return the caller's worktree root**, not the family root, or the fleet model can
   never be runtime-isolated (F4).
4. **Promote an adversarial pass into `verify`**, or make an audit capability a fleet
   precondition — it caught what nothing else did (G3).
5. **Either give `resolve_routing` the ability to change an outcome, or drop it from the shipper
   path** (F6).
6. **State Article 2's unattended exception**, instead of shipping a constitution the flagship
   skill contradicts by design (G1).
7. **Persist task artifacts outside the worktree** — a run whose process record dies with a
   `git worktree prune` has no audit trail (F8).
8. **Re-test the §10 list and delete whatever is already fixed** from the dispatch-brief lore.

## 12. Caveats

- **Defect counts, verify verdicts, and the 25-brief-error figure are run-reported.** They were
  not re-derived from the diffs; a shipper counting its own adversarial findings is the same
  self-certification pattern this document criticises elsewhere. They are cited as claims.
- **Cost is the session statusline's figure**, not a re-derived token accounting. The method in
  [fleet-run-token-accounting.md](./fleet-run-token-accounting.md) warns the obvious reading
  over-reports by ~2×; that method was **not** applied here.
- **No control arm exists.** Nothing in this run establishes what the same model would have
  produced from the same 4 000-word dispatch brief *without* wf — which is precisely the
  question `plugins/wf-sandbox-testing/` exists to answer, and this run did not ask it.
- **Single run, single project, single registry** (`git, linear`). Findings about inert
  degradation generalize; findings about worktree behaviour are entangled with this host.
- Transcripts are machine-local and prunable; the 16 subject worktrees were still present at
  the time of writing and hold the only copy of 15 task artifact sets.
